subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining work fix the scheduled producer that asks for bad paths, change generic read-tool semantics for directories/date paths, or wait for live RSS proof before changing behavior?
rationale: Source inspection shows partial fixes and a remaining model-facing tool-contract question; automation cannot safely choose between producer repair and broader read-tool behavior changes without maintainer intent.

options.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
options.body: Confirm the current scheduled path with stability diagnostics and patch the scheduler, heartbeat, or memory prompt/source that asks for `memory-system/CORE.md` or directory reads.

options.title: Accept scoped read-tool fallbacks
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally broaden read-tool behavior, such as a directory listing or daily-memory redirect, but should treat that as a model-facing compatibility decision.

options.title: Wait for stronger live proof
options.body: Keep the issue in manual review until a current-build log bundle or stability snapshot proves the RSS growth mechanism.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
recommendation.body: Confirm the current scheduled path with stability diagnostics and patch the scheduler, heartbeat, or memory prompt/source that asks for `memory-system/CORE.md` or directory reads.
